## Class Materials

* [**R Cheat Sheet: every function in this course**](https://github.com/evictionresearch/SOC-N100-Housing-Precarity-2026/blob/main/code/r_functions_cheatsheet.R) — `code/r_functions_cheatsheet.R`, already on your DataHub. One line + one example for every function the labs use, grouped by task, tagged with the lab where you first meet it. Keep it open in an RStudio tab and Ctrl-F it.
* [R Coding Resources](learn_r.qmd)
* Tidycensus Book: [Analyzing U.S. Census Data: Methods, Maps, and Models in R](https://walker-data.com/census-r/index.html)
* [Datawrapper.de](https://www.datawrapper.de/)

## Other datasets or data points

* [HUD Fair Market Rent (FMR), FY2026](https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr/fmrs/FY2026_code/2026summary.odn)
* [Apartmentlist.com monthly rents](https://www.apartmentlist.com/research/category/data-rent-estimates)
* [Consumer Price Index (CPI) calculator](https://www.bls.gov/data/inflation_calculator.htm)
* [Tim's neighborhood package](https://github.com/evictionresearch/neighborhood). This helps create segregated census tracts for any area using tidycensus.
